issues.detail: Covers only the happy path for four primitives and omits error and edge cases such as controlled open state, async confirm handlers, forceMount/animation exit handling, SSR hydration issues, and the Dialog/Dropdown focus-return interaction.

The two examples only restate which Step component to reuse with a one-line expected result, and the Example 2 `onSelect` handler is not wired into the `UserMenu` code, so they are not full realistic demonstrations.

scenarios.name: delete-confirm-dialog-a11y
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric directly: it uses Dialog.Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay and Content, Dialog.Close asChild for Cancel, VisuallyHidden around Dialog.Title, and Dialog.Description with an aria-describedby={undefined} note. B uses AlertDialog (Cancel/Action) instead of Dialog and Dialog.Close, so it misses the specific components the rubric names, though its accessibility handling is sound.

scenarios.name: menu-keep-open-onselect
scenarios.rationale: Both use onSelect with preventDefault on Copy link, leave Sign out without preventDefault, and note 'use client'; B adds a working copy handler and state and an extra Server Action tip, but A's explanation is also correct and complete, so B is only slightly ahead.

scenarios.name: tabs-and-tooltips-toolbar
scenarios.rationale: Both responses satisfy every rubric item (Tabs.Root with defaultValue, Tabs.List/Trigger/Content, data-[state=active] styling, Tooltip.Provider delayDuration={300}, Root/Trigger asChild/Portal/Content, and aria-label), but A uses a real Lucide icon with aria-hidden and the standard individual packages, whereas B uses an emoji as the icon and the unified radix-ui package, which is slightly less polished though valid.
